comment: The building blocks baldssl implements, shown on the website. Each pull request that implements one sets its status to `implemented` (and its `link` to the pull request). Statuses: implemented, in-progress, planned.

primitives.name: Base64, PEM and DER reading
primitives.purpose: Decoding certificates and keys: canonical base64, PEM framing, and a strict DER reader that rejects non-canonical encodings.

primitives.name: SHA-1 and SHA-2
primitives.purpose: Fingerprints, and the hashes signatures are computed over (FIPS 180-4).

primitives.name: Randomness from the operating system
primitives.purpose: Key and nonce generation; the only code allowed to use unsafe.

primitives.name: Constant-time prime fields
primitives.purpose: Arithmetic modulo the primes of P-256, P-384, P-521 and Ed25519, without branches on secret values.

primitives.name: P-256, P-384 and P-521
primitives.purpose: The NIST curves by model (affine, projective with complete formulas, Jacobian) and constant-time scalar multiplication.

primitives.name: Ed25519
primitives.purpose: The Edwards curve of Ed25519 and the derivation of a public key from a private key (RFC 8032).

primitives.name: DER writer
primitives.purpose: Encoding ASN.1 structures: keys now, certificate requests and certificates next.

primitives.name: Private keys (PKCS#8)
primitives.purpose: Generating keys and writing them as openssl genpkey does.

primitives.name: ECDSA
primitives.purpose: Signing and verifying with P-256, P-384 and P-521 (FIPS 186-5), for certificate requests, signing and verification.
